paper_metadata.title: Effect of B addition on the microstructure, mechanical properties, and corrosion behavior of Ti-24Nb-4Zr-2Mn alloys

evidence.quote: In the present study, (Ti, Nb)B reinforced Ti-Nb-Zr-Mn alloys were successfully fabricated through ball milling and spark plasma sintering (SPS) process with the addition of TiB2.

the effects of B on the microstructure, mechanical properties, and corrosion resistance of the TNZM alloys were systematically investigated. After the addition of TiB2, the (Ti, Nb)B reinforcement phase was in situ formed.

property_observations.property: yield strength increase due to grain refinement

evidence.quote: The calculation results show that the increase in strengthening due to grain refinement is not high (∼56 MPa).
An extremely small amount of the added B element was dissolved in the Ti matrix to form solid solution, which had a certain solid solution strengthening effect.
As the content of the B element increased, the uniformly dispersed precipitated phases could not only effectively refine the matrix structure but also played a role in dispersion strengthening.
The (Ti, Nb)B precipitates in the TNZMB alloys show a precipitation hardening effect, which is beneficial for increasing the strength of the alloy.
The average grain size of the alloy gradually decreases from ~ 27 μm to ~ 12 μm, which can be ascribed to the refinement of the TiB phase [20].
They also act as stress raisers, making them the crack initiation sites for fracture. As a result, the ductility of the alloys decreases as the content of (Ti, Nb)B increases.
Considering that the solubility of B in the Ti solid solution is extremely low, the solid solution strengthening effect of B can be neglected.
The pinning effect of the (Ti, Nb)B precipitated phases promotes grain refinement.
Thus, the precipitation strengthening of (Ti, Nb)B is the most dominant factor.
The excellent interfacial bonding, combined with the favorable CTE match, facilitates highly efficient load transfer, establishing it as the dominant strengthening mechanism.
